payload.name: Preference-memory pass for activity-enhancement answers
payload.description: When a question asks which ways or items people use to enhance an activity and event/state memories suggest candidate items, search each named person's preference memories for those items before answering.
content: If a question asks what ways/items people use to enhance an activity (e.g., yoga practice), collect candidate item names from retrieved event/state memories.
For each person named in the question, run one additional hybrid search combining the activity, the candidate item terms, and preference phrasing (prefers, likes, uses); use a modest top_k (e.g., 5).
Stop after one such preference-focused search per person returns the item-specific preferences; do not expand synonyms beyond already-observed candidate items.

solves: Preference memories that state which items people use to enrich an activity (e.g., candles, scents, oils, music) are often missed by queries paraphrased around 'enhance practice', leaving answers incomplete. Applies to future questions asking what ways or items people use to enhance a named activity, when event memories already show candidate items; then run one preference-focused search per named person with those item terms. Does not apply when the question is a direct preference query (default preference retrieval suffices) or when no activity-enhancement items are involved.
